newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: JCI in Southern Africa iron ore study.
newsitem.headline: JCI in Southern Africa iron ore study.

text.p: JCI Ltd confirmed on Friday that it will participate in a feasibility study into a proposed three billion rand iron ore project in Zimbabwe and Mozambique.
"South African mining company JCI Ltd is pleased to announce that it will be participating in the feasibility study into the proposed Beira Iron Project," the group said in a statement.
The study was due to be launched on Friday in Maputo.
The project plans to mine and beneficiate iron ore in Zimbabwe and rail it to the border with Mozambique where it would be reduced using natural gas from Mozambique's Temane gas fields.
The product, hot briquetted iron, would then be exported through the established port of Beira.
"Should the project proceed it will comprise a combined investment in Zimbabwe and Mozambique of between two and three billion rands.
In addition to the governments of Mozambique and Zimbabwe, the major project partners are JCI Projects, a division of JCI Ltd, and Atlantic Richfield Corporation (ARCO).
